powers.name: Sidestep
powers.description: Move exactly 1 hex in any direction. It provokes nothing, and the destination’s terrain cost is irrelevant — step into a hex costing 1, 2 or 3 alike. Costs no Stamina, and it is usable every other Turn. It is a bonus move, so it does NOT add your Movement stat. Paladins only.
powers.intent: The free half-step, and the drawback is the wait. On the Turn it is down you can be pinned, which is the whole reason it has a cooldown.
powers.source: 2026-08-17. Universal — every hero starts with Move and Sidestep. | 2026-08-17 : enemies have it too. This is the rule that makes zones of control soft. | 2026-08-21: Sidestep gets a cooldown of 1 — "it does break this statement of 'it's always available.' No, it's available every other turn." Enemies lose it entirely (engine/DECISIONS.md 2026-08-21: an enemy carries exactly ONE movement power in its data row). Split into two: Sidestep is free but every other Turn; Side Roll costs 1 Stamina but is always there. Rogues and Rangers take Side Roll by default, everyone else Sidestep. Beasts and Civilians get NEITHER. | 2026-08-21: "Leap. It'll move you two squares with no attacks of opportunity given. Cost 2 stamina. And give you +2 Strength until the end of your activation. And this one goes on a Warrior. And let's remove the one we gave to Priest and Mage, they both don't get one." Sidestep narrows to the Paladin — the Warrior took Leap instead, and Mage and Priest now get nothing. | 2026-08-21: the BONUS MOVE family. "Mage gets Focus. It actually does zero movement, zero stamina cost. They gain one stamina. Priest gets Devotion. Does zero movement. They lose 1 maximum stamina, and they gain 2 stamina." A bonus move IS your movement for the Activation — you pick Move, a Flight, or your bonus move, never two. "Only the full movement actions and things like them benefit from the Move stat, so all of these bonus moves do not benefit from the Move stat." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched.

powers.name: Leap
powers.description: Move exactly 2 hexes in any direction. It provokes nothing, and the destination’s terrain cost is irrelevant. You gain +2 Strength until the end of the Turn. It costs 2 Stamina and there is no cooldown. It is a bonus move, so it does NOT add your Movement stat. Warriors only.
powers.intent: The only movement power that is an opening rather than an escape. Two hexes gets you INTO the fight and the Strength lands on the swing you take when you arrive. It rides your attacks of opportunity for the rest of the Turn too, once those exist — a Warrior who leaps into the middle punishes everything that walks past.
powers.source: 2026-08-21: "Leap. It'll move you two squares with no attacks of opportunity given. Cost 2 stamina. And give you +2 Strength until the end of your activation. And this one goes on a Warrior. And let's remove the one we gave to Priest and Mage, they both don't get one." | 2026-08-21 : "isn’t the end of activation the same as the end of this turn? powers.name: Ground layers
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE. A hex carries at most one status, and applying a new one removes and replaces whatever was there — curse a burning hex to 1 Weak and the hex flips from Burn to Weak, it does not hold both. The single exception is Burn and Frost, which cancel one for one instead of replacing (rule.burn-frost-cancel): frost laid on a burning hex subtracts from it rather than swapping it. Ground layers are persistent — they carry no clock of their own. The four layers are: burning · frost · poisoned · darkness. Darkness as a layer is the localised kind a unit paints on the board — distinct from Darkness the battlefield condition, which covers the whole map. The night family (2026-09-02) is what made the distinction load-bearing: those units paint darkness in radii around themselves.
powers.intent: The ground is a state, not a countdown. Frost put out a fire because it took the hex, not because it cancelled anything.
powers.source: 2026-08-20: "Status effects on terrain are just persistent. No turn tracking, just it is burning or it is frost. The only thing that should replace a ground layer effect is if a different one is applied, it replaces the previous one. The ground can only have one effect on it, and that effect stays." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched. | Ruled 2026-09-02. Verbatim: "All ground effects, remove and replace, except Burn and Frost which counter. So if i curse a ground to add 1 weak, but it had burn. It flips from Burn to Weak. So each ground tile can only have 1 status on it." | 2026-09-02: the four layers enumerated on the row, darkness included.

powers.name: Summon order
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. Every summoned unit is given a summon number when it arrives — the first thing summoned is 1, the second is 2, and so on, counted separately for each side. In its own Phase, summoned units activate FIRST, in summon-number order, BEFORE any unit that was already on the field. Summoned heroes go first in the Hero Phase; summoned enemies go first in the Enemy Phase.
powers.intent: A summon that arrives and then waits behind everything else is a summon that did nothing. Going first is most of what you paid for.
powers.source: 2026-08-20. Written ahead of the summoning system itself, which does not exist yet — see engine/COMBAT-SEQUENCE.md #Summoning. | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched.

powers.name: Enemy attacks are defined, and melee is the floor
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. Every enemy states its attacks explicitly, by attack id — an enemy with no attack listed is unfinished content, not an enemy that cannot swing. If an enemy has no melee attack among them, it carries attack.basic.melee: Strength +0, melee reach, no stamina. A ranged enemy still has it, for when something closes.
powers.intent: Nothing on the board is ever unable to act. A caster shoved into melee swings for Strength; it does not stand there empty-handed.
powers.source: 2026-08-30: "every enemy needs its attacks clearly defined. If it does not have a melee attack, an enemy has a basic melee S+0 damage attack." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched.

powers.name: Nothing outlasts the Battle
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. No effect in the game persists past the end of the Battle — not a stat change, not a status, not a drain, not a scar. The longest any effect can last is the rest of the Battle, which is the first of the four durations. "Permanent" in any entry means permanent WITHIN the Battle and nothing more; an effect that would carry into the next Battle does not exist.
powers.intent: The Battle is the unit of consequence. A hero who ends one drained is whole at the start of the next, and content never has to reason about state it cannot see.
powers.source: 2026-08-31: "There's no permanent past the end of battle for anything." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched.

powers.name: A status magnitude is a value
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. Any status a unit is carrying may be read as a NUMBER by damage or by another effect — "Strength + 2 x the target's Root" is legal, and so is scaling a duration, a heal or a chance off a status the target already has. This holds for every status, not a named few.
powers.intent: It gives every status a second life. A debuff you applied three Phases ago is still worth something because the next attack reads it.
powers.source: 2026-09-01: "All of them or status effects can also be used to change the scale of damage or effect." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched.

powers.name: Forced movement is Knockback and Pull
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. There are exactly THREE forced-movement verbs: Knockback, which pushes a unit directly away from the source; Pull, which draws it directly toward the source; and DRIVE, which is a Knockback in which THE ATTACKER ALSO MOVES FORWARD — the target is pushed and the attacker advances into the hex it left. All three take a number of hexes and all three run on ONE axis: nothing moves sideways. No fourth verb.
powers.intent: Two opposed verbs, one axis. The 2026-08-20 cut left only Knockback because Pull had arrived as a bespoke system for one power; reinstated 2026-09-01 as a first-class verb with a real roster behind it.
powers.source: 2026-09-01: "Yep, I'm adding pull back in. It's a reversal." Reverses the 2026-08-20 ruling "the pull is cut. Knockback is the only forced movement in the game." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched. | 2026-09-01: the 'no third verb' clause is SUPERSEDED. Drive added, verbatim: 'Drive is knockback, but the attacker also moves forward.'

powers.name: Limits stop stacking; options need no limit
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. The per-unit limits on Armor, Idols, Blood Runes and Relics exist for ONE reason: to stop every item slot being additive in the same direction. A hero may not wear five defensive things. Trinkets carry no such limit because a trinket gives an OPTION — a thing you can do — not a bigger number, so five of them buy five choices rather than five stacks. The authoring test is therefore: if it is additive it belongs in a limited category; if it is an option it can be a trinket. The one deliberate exception is a status IMMUNITY, which is additive but conditional: it is often worth nothing, so its value is the pre-battle question of who should carry it today. That is a War Council decision, not a stack, and immunities stay trinkets. THE CATEGORY LADDER, ruled 2026-09-02: armor is the single greatest stat gain available and an armor with no downside is the category working, not a fault; idols and blood runes are narrower, smaller gains; relics swap; trinkets buy options. The limits exist so that a large gain is bounded by being ONE armor, ONE idol, ONE rune, ONE relic — not so that every category must hurt.
powers.intent: It makes item slots a COVERAGE budget rather than a power budget. Handing a hero another slot makes them more flexible, not stronger — which is why slots can grow generously without inflating anything.
powers.source: 2026-09-02: "The reason for the Idol, Blood Rune / Armor / Relic limits are to prevent EVERY item slot from being additive in any direction. So I can't just add 5 defensive things. Because the Trinkets mostly give options, they don't need that limit." And on the exception: "I intentionally had immunities as an exception, because they are useless often, [I] want it in planning. OK, I can use my immunity — on whom? Is a good, non-permanent choice in battle prep." | Merged onto the trunk from the parallel chat 2026-09-02; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling. | 2026-09-02, verbatim: 'Armor is not a trade-off category. It is a massive upside category. It can have trade-offs. It is the single greatest stat gain that you can have. Then idols and Bloodrune are also stat gains, but they are of a narrower dynamic and less than armor.' | 2026-09-02: the weapons-vs-blood-runes distinction added after a review priced a weapon rider against a rune rider.
powers.categoryLadder: Stat gain, largest to smallest: ARMOR (the biggest gain in the game; may carry a trade-off, is not defined by one) > IDOLS and BLOOD RUNES (gains, narrower and less than armor) > RELICS (swaps — the gain is paid for on another axis) > TRINKETS (options, not numbers). Ruled 2026-09-02.
powers.weaponsVsRunes: RULED 2026-09-02: 'Weapons are fundamentally different than Bloodrunes because Bloodrunes add on top.' A weapon's payload is what that weapon DOES INSTEAD of what another weapon would do — you carry one, and its riders are the reason to carry it rather than the alternative. A blood rune ADDS ITS PAYLOAD ON TOP of whatever weapon is already there, so the same number on a rune is strictly additional power while on a weapon it is a choice. THE TWO MAY NOT BE PRICED AGAINST EACH OTHER. A 2026-09-02 review compared the Daggers' 50 Surge on kill against rune.avatar-of-war's +20 and called the weapon overpowered; that comparison was invalid and the Daggers' rider stands.

powers.name: All healing comes from one function
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. There is ONE heal in the game and every source routes through it — a power, an item, a trigger, a lifesteal rider, and REGENERATION, which does not heal by a private path of its own but calls the same function at End of Phase. Anything that modifies healing therefore modifies all of it, once, in one place: Karma raises the amount, Burn halves it. Content never has to say which kinds of healing it means, because there is only one kind. THE STATIONS RUN IN ORDER: base -> all bonuses (Karma and any other) -> Burn halves -> applied to Health, and half the applied amount comes off Bleed. Regeneration calls this function like everything else, so a Regeneration tick is healed, halved and Bleed-stripping exactly as a cast heal is.
powers.intent: It turns three special cases into one pipeline. Karma boosting heals, Burn halving them and Regeneration ticking are not three rules that happen to touch health — they are stations on a single function, and a new modifier is written once instead of per source.
powers.source: 2026-09-02: "Regeneration should CAUSE healing, healing should all come from same function." Answers the open question from the healing-cures-Bleed decision: Regeneration IS healing received, so everything true of a heal is true of a Regeneration tick. | Merged onto the trunk from the parallel chat 2026-09-02; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling. | 2026-09-02, the station order ruled verbatim: 'karma and bonuses to healing before Burn, then halved, then applied'. This was the one thing rule.one-healing-function left open.
powers.stations: THE ORDER, ruled 2026-09-02: (1) the base heal; (2) ALL BONUSES TO HEALING, Karma included, are added; (3) Burn HALVES the result; (4) what remains is applied to Health — and half of that applied amount is removed from Bleed (rounded nearest, 0.5 up). Bonuses before the halving, always: Karma 3 on a Regeneration 4 tick with Burn present heals (4+3)/2 = 4 (rounds nearest, 0.5 up), and sheds 2 Bleed.

powers.name: Burn and Frost cancel
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE. Burn and Frost annihilate each other one for one, at the moment either is applied — a unit never carries both. Apply 2 Burn to a unit holding 1 Frost and it ends on 1 Burn; apply 1 Frost to that unit and it ends on 0. The same cancellation is the ONE exception to ground layers replacing each other (rule.ground-layers).
powers.intent: Fire and ice are the only pair in the game that argue instead of taking turns.
powers.source: Ruled 2026-09-02. Verbatim: "Do you have a note that Frost and Burn counter each other. Add 2 burn to a target with 1 Frost, you end up with 1 Burn. Add a frost to that unit and you end up with 0."

powers.name: Corpses
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE. A CORPSE is a board object, and it is what every raise, summon, consume and feed in the game reads. Corpses are created when any enemy is DOWNED and when a hero actually DIES (the deathbed check fails, or the bleed-out clock runs out). FOUR THINGS DENY ONE, and denying a corpse is the counter to the whole undead economy: (1) DESTROY CORPSE — an on-kill effect, mostly a hero ability, that destroys the body as it falls; (2) SUMMONS NEVER LEAVE ONE, so a zombie raised from a corpse leaves nothing when it dies and the loop cannot feed itself; (3) OBLITERATION by Shadow reaching Max Health removes the unit with no corpse (status.shadow); (4) an effect that consumes corpses removes them outright. A denied corpse stops raising, stops summoning, stops the Escalating Demon, and stops anything else that feeds on bodies.
powers.intent: The undead do not have a damage problem, they have a supply problem. This is the supply.
powers.source: RULED: corpse creation 2026-08-25 ('Corpses are created by any enemy that gets downed and any hero that actually dies', with the bleed-out timer). DESTROY CORPSE and the summons clause were dictated 2026-08-30 (DESIGN-DUMP-CLEANED.md §9) and had never reached the pipeline — landed 2026-09-02 when it was asked for. Obliteration joins them from the same day's Shadow ruling. capability.corpses in gen/enemies-authored.json is the engine-side name for the board object.

powers.name: Stealth does not hold
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE. At the End of every Phase, one random stealthed unit may be revealed — either side. The chance is 10% PER STEALTHED UNIT ON THE BOARD, with a floor of 25%: one hidden unit is a 25% chance, five is 50%, ten is certain. It reads the board as it stands, never any history. The more of the field is hidden, the less the hiding holds.
powers.intent: You cannot win by waiting, and a board full of hidden things cannot stay hidden.
powers.needsCapability: capability.stealth — designed in COMBAT-DESIGN (a stealth unit cannot be targeted and does not appear on the map), not yet built.
powers.source: Dictated 2026-09-02. REFRAMED at landing. Dictated as "if there are two full turns of no attack actions, one random stealth unit gets revealed" — which counts turns of history, and content is banned from occurrence counting and event history (R25). Ruled: rethink it. This is the history-free shape with the same intent — a per-Phase chance rather than a stall detector. It is strictly simpler and it also makes stealth a resource that burns. THE TRADE: it fires even in a busy battle, so stealth is temporary always rather than only when the battle stalls. Say so if the stall condition was the point. | 2026-09-02, softened, then scaled by ruling: 'Give it a 25% chance that one random stealth unit is revealed at the end of every phase.' The certain per-Phase reveal was mine and too harsh — a 25% roll leaves stealth worth taking while still making it temporary. The roll needs its own named stream (Law 4), keyed by what the roll is. | 2026-09-02, second pass, verbatim: 'It is either a 25% chance, or it is a 10% chance per unit. If there are 10 units that are stealth, one will be revealed. If there are 5 units that are stealth, there is a 50% chance. If there is 1 unit that is stealth, it will be a 25% chance.' So the chance is the HIGHER of 25 and 10 x count — the floor keeps a lone hider from being safe, the scaling keeps a screen of ten from holding. Counting units on the board is present state, not event history, so it stays clear of the R25 ban.
powers.formula: max(25, 10 x the number of stealthed units on the board), capped at 100

statuses.name: Karma
statuses.effect: Increases every heal the unit receives by its value, and every point of damage it deals by half its value.
statuses.decay: No clock: -1 on a kill, and nothing else.
statuses.source: 2026-08-20. The only status that decays on an event rather than on the clock. RE-RULED IDENTICALLY 2026-08-25, verbatim: "Karma increases healing and increases damage by half of the Karma value. So it increases healing to the target that has karma by the amount of karma. And one half of the Karma value is added to all damage. Karma is lost whenever the unit kills another unit. So, every unit, during player attack, if there is a kill, there is a check to see if there is karma, and if there is, it goes down by one." | Ruled 2026-09-02. Verbatim: "Karma does not tick down at end of activation, so ACTUALLY its order doesn't matter. There is no decrease Karma stage during settling. That should happen during the onKill settling from damage." | 2026-09-02: cut to ONE SENTENCE, ruled — a status row teaches the status, it does not narrate what one item does with it. The previous multi-sentence text is kept as longEffect for the Codex, not as the definition.
statuses.longEffect: While you carry Karma: every heal you receive is increased by your Karma, and every point of damage you deal is increased by HALF your Karma, rounded down.

statuses.name: Slow
statuses.effect: Reduces the unit's Movement by its value.
statuses.source: 2026-08-20: "clean up that movement stuff." Fourteen entries said "the target loses N Movement on its next Turn" — one meaning, two wordings, and the only per-target clock left in the game. It is a status now, so it decays on the same ladder as everything else and nothing has to remember whose next Turn it is. | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched. | 2026-09-02: cut to ONE SENTENCE, ruled — a status row teaches the status, it does not narrate what one item does with it. The previous multi-sentence text is kept as longEffect for the Codex, not as the definition.
statuses.longEffect: While you carry Slow, your Movement is reduced by your Slow.

statuses.name: Taunt
statuses.effect: Forces the taunted unit to target whoever taunted it.
statuses.source: 2026-09-01: "Taunt takes hero control away from the player when it's used by an enemy. Taunt, when used by a hero, makes the enemy fixate on the hero." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched. | 2026-09-02: cut to ONE SENTENCE, ruled — a status row teaches the status, it does not narrate what one item does with it. The previous multi-sentence text is kept as longEffect for the Codex, not as the definition.
statuses.longEffect: Cuts both ways by who applied it. A HERO taunting an enemy makes that hero the enemy's priority target in AI selection while the Taunt lasts — the enemy fixates. An ENEMY taunting a hero takes the hero away from the player: it becomes AI-driven, activates FIRST in the Hero Phase, prioritises the unit that taunted it, and the rest of the party acts afterwards.

statuses.name: Dazed
statuses.effect: Takes the unit out of its owner's control and hands it to the AI.
statuses.source: 2026-09-01: "Dazed, used on a hero, causes the player to lose control of it, the same as a taunt, for a number of turns... it just means the player loses control and the unit is going to behave the way it would in the simulation with the AI for that striker type." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched. | 2026-09-02: cut to ONE SENTENCE, ruled — a status row teaches the status, it does not narrate what one item does with it. The previous multi-sentence text is kept as longEffect for the Codex, not as the definition.
statuses.longEffect: The player loses control of the hero for as long as it lasts. Unlike Taunt there is no priority target — the unit simply behaves as the AI would drive its striker type.

It does two different things: there is a critical effect, and then there is a status effect. Do we need to disambiguate this right now, or can you account for that?" Accounted for as two ids: status.dazed keeps the Sep 1 meaning; the chart's row applies THIS status. The id and name are a plain descriptive PLACEHOLDER chosen so nothing is invented — rename in one place (this row and the chart's compile in mkenginepack.mjs) whenever a real name is given. Attacks and movement are untouched; only class powers are refused.

statuses.name: Confusion
statuses.effect: Swaps the affected unit's AI strategy for a different one.
statuses.source: 2026-09-01: "Confusion inflicted on an enemy causes it to use a different AI strategy." | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched. | 2026-09-02: cut to ONE SENTENCE, ruled — a status row teaches the status, it does not narrate what one item does with it. The previous multi-sentence text is kept as longEffect for the Codex, not as the definition.
statuses.longEffect: Inflicted on an enemy, it swaps that enemy's AI strategy for a different one while it lasts.

statuses.name: Root
statuses.effect: Stops the unit moving at all.

Root also has a customer that scales off its magnitude (the Spider's Chomp), which rule.status-as-a-value makes legal. | Merged onto the trunk 2026-09-01 from the parallel content chat; attribution de-named per the standing passive-voice ruling, wording and dates untouched. | 2026-09-02: cut to ONE SENTENCE, ruled — a status row teaches the status, it does not narrate what one item does with it. The previous multi-sentence text is kept as longEffect for the Codex, not as the definition.
statuses.longEffect: While you carry Root you CANNOT MOVE AT ALL — not a reduction, a stop. Movement actions and bonus moves alike are unavailable for as long as it lasts.

statuses.name: Bleed
statuses.effect: Deals TRUE damage equal to its value each Turn, and healing removes half the amount healed.
statuses.curedBy: Healing received removes Bleed equal to HALF the healing (rounded nearest, 0.5 up). Regeneration is healing (rule.one-healing-function), so a Regeneration tick strips Bleed too. Burn halves healing received first, so the Bleed removal is half of what actually landed — a burning unit sheds a quarter of what it otherwise would.
statuses.source: Ruled 2026-09-02. Verbatim: "Bleed is True Damage." and "Bleed is being converted to magnitude damage. Also healing should cure bleed. Regen should be healing." SUPERSEDES the old flat model (N was a turn count, each tick a flat 2). This also closes the standing "does Armor touch Bleed?" question: it does not — nothing does. | 2026-09-02: cut to ONE SENTENCE, ruled — a status row teaches the status, it does not narrate what one item does with it. The previous multi-sentence text is kept as longEffect for the Codex, not as the definition.
statuses.longEffect: N TRUE damage at End of Phase, then −1. True damage, so neither Armor nor Resist touches it — that is what "Bleed is never resisted" always meant, now said in one word.

statuses.name: Frost
statuses.effect: Adds its value to every physical hit the unit receives, per hit.
statuses.application: Applied like Burn. Burn and Frost annihilate one for one on application (rule.burn-frost-cancel) — a unit never carries both.
statuses.source: RULED 2026-09-02, verbatim: 'Frost should ADD to physical damage. Then its order of ticking down in settling also doesn't matter, but it can go first.' and 'Frost is applied like Burn.' Direction (incoming), scope (all physical, not melee only) and per-hit application ruled the same day. Ends the two-week gap in which content referenced Frost with no definition. | 2026-09-02: cut to ONE SENTENCE, ruled — a status row teaches the status, it does not narrate what one item does with it. The previous multi-sentence text is kept as longEffect for the Codex, not as the definition.
statuses.longEffect: A unit carrying Frost N takes +N on EVERY physical hit it receives — all physical, melee and ranged alike, and PER HIT: a two-swing attack against Frost 3 takes +3 on each swing, +6 in total. Frost deals no damage of its own; it is the mirror of Armor, which subtracts from the same number. Bleed beats Resist by being true; Frost beats Armor by outgrowing it.

statuses.name: Shadow
statuses.effect: Obliterates the unit — killed, removed, no corpse — once it reaches the unit's Max Health.
statuses.decay: It GROWS: +1 per Turn, first of everything in Settling. It never decays.
statuses.source: RULED 2026-09-02, verbatim: 'Shadow, ticks UP during settling (first), then is compared to max health. If shadow = max health, unit is obliterated. (killed, removed from field, no corpse).' Tick size (+1) and the at-or-above threshold ruled the same day. Shadow was named 2026-09-01 with no effect anywhere — this is its first definition, and the last unshaped status is now shaped. | 2026-09-02: cut to ONE SENTENCE, ruled — a status row teaches the status, it does not narrate what one item does with it. The previous multi-sentence text is kept as longEffect for the Codex, not as the definition.
statuses.longEffect: Shadow does nothing on its own. It TICKS UP — first of everything in Settling — and is then compared to the unit's Max Health. The moment Shadow is AT OR ABOVE Max Health the unit is OBLITERATED: killed, removed from the field, and NO CORPSE is left. It is the only effect in the game that denies a corpse, which is what makes it worth fearing rather than merely surviving.

statuses.name: Protection
statuses.decay: Spent by the damage it prevents, and decreases by an additional 1 per Turn.
statuses.source: RE-RULED 2026-09-02, verbatim: 'Protection prevents damage from any source. Decreases by an additional 1 point per turn.' The previous row over-explained a core mechanic across four fields; a core mechanic gets one line.

Clearly differentiated: test- typeIds, (TEST) names, never ships. The engine reads these through the generated pack (mkenginepack.mjs) — nothing hand-typed engine-side. alphaTeam.note: THE ALPHA TEAM, dictated 2026-08-27: "take those heroes and make them the way they are supposed to actually be in content" — the test cohort rebuilt on the real scaffolding. Same stat bodies (copied from testCohort, which copied live heroes 2026-08-20), one hero per class, but armed through kit -> authored items -> authored attack rows instead of the engine's six PROVISIONAL attacks. Test-only statuses translated into the vocabulary: ward->protection, hobble->slow, enfeeble->weak. Punch arrives via universalToAllUnits, never listed. Movement powers are derived from class by the converter. Clearly differentiated: alpha- typeIds, (ALPHA) names, never ships. Arcane Bolt is NOT carried over — the Air Mage's ability is now the Lightning Staff's, as a real item grant.

One chart for all damage types, fully symmetric. Entry point name fixed in GLOSSARY.md: rollCritEffect. Row keys exist so event-log lines can name their cause (Law 12) — keys, not content ids.

statusFamilies.note: Named 2026-09-02, and the Bleed conversion is what made the split clean. MAGNITUDE: N is how much. DURATION: N is how long — and that family is forced, because "cannot move" has no magnitude. Bleed was never an inconsistency; it was a magnitude status wearing a duration number, and it has been moved to the family it belonged in. rule.status-as-a-value reads a status's number either way — the family says what the number means.
